headline: Approved a request that the City Manager consider a City Council budget priority process; proposed meeting-time and public comment rule changes were placed on file.
summary: Councilors also discussed three proposed budget rules and approved the September 28 minutes. Proposed changes to council meeting start times and public comment time were placed on file, along with a review of Rule Five on special meetings. The City Clerk was asked to add Rule 35 language to the council agenda.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the September 28, 2026 meeting, 3-0.
Approved a request that the City Manager consider a City Council budget priority process, 3-0.
Placed on file the budget priority order, 3-0.
Placed on file proposed changes to Rule 4 and Rule 39, setting a 5:30 p.m. meeting start and 60 minutes of public comment, 3-0.
Placed on file a review of Rule Five on calling special meetings, 3-0.
Approved a request that the City Clerk include Rule 35 language under the Orders section of the City Council agenda, 3-0.

. Communication of the City Manager 3 
November 9, 2026 Page 3 of 12Municipal and Legislative Operations Committee
Transmitting Informational Communication Relative to Proposed New Rules 61, 62, and 
63 of the Rules of City Council.
# 9.26A CM October 13, 2026
a.
November 9, 2026 Page 4 of 12Municipal and Legislative Operations Committee
Chairperson Councilor Mitra read the item and recognized the Chief Financial Officer, who provided 
an overview analyzing the potential impact of implementing three (3) proposed new Rules of City 
Council, Rules 61, 62, and 63.  
Chairperson Councilor Mitra highlighted the importance of City Councilors having the opportunity to 
provide the City Manager with preliminary fiscal year priorities. 
Chairperson Councilor Mitra recognized the City Clerk, who provided an overview of a 1989 change 
to the Rules of City Council proposed by Former At -Large City Councilor Raymond V. Mariano to 
assign standing committees specific departments for budget oversight and a history of preliminary 
fiscal year budgets, goals and objectives reported to City Council by Former City Managers William 
Mulford and Thomas R. Hoover.
Chairperson Councilor Mitra recognized Councilor Bergman, who discussed the estimated twenty 
(20) to twenty -five (25) department heads that submit budgets to the Department of Administration 
and Finance, timelines associated with the department receiving city department budgets, the process 
relative for the department to review and present the fiscal year budget to the City Manager , 
timelines associated with the City Manager providing a first in -depth budget review, April as last 
opportunity the City Manager has to  adjust the budget prior to its transmission to City Council, and 
the feasibility of the City Manager meeting with City Councilors in April to discuss last budget 
adjustment opportunities with the Chief Financial Officer. 
Chairperson Councilor Mitra highlighted the importance of City Council’s involvement in reviewing 
draft fiscal year budgets with the Chief Financial Officer. 
Chairperson Councilor Mitra then discussed creating a comprehensive Rule 61, which would include 
language outlined in the originally proposed Rules 61, 62, and 63, with the exception of amending the 
date from March 1 to February 15 for City Councilors to provide budget priorities and 
recommendations to the City Manager. 
Chairperson Councilor Mitra recognized Councilor Rosen, who discussed Chairperson Councilor 
Mitra’s comprehensive Rule 61 recommendation, the feasibility of moving for a Chairman’s Order to 
request the notion of a comprehensive Rule 61 as an order to the City Manager, and the feasibility of 
City Councilors transmitting orders to request standing committees invite appropriate department 
representatives within the jurisdiction of each committee to hearings for the purpose of discussing 
department budget priorities with the City Clerk.
Chairperson Councilor Mitra recognized Councilor Rosen, who spoke concerning the item. 
Chairperson Councilor Mitra recognized Councilor Economou, who discussed the approximate two 
million dollars ($2,000,000.00) of available discretionary funding, the process relative for the Budget 
Division to create a status quo budget, and economic reasons preliminary budgets had been brought 
forward to City Council with the Chief Financial Officer and City Clerk.
Chairperson Councilor Mitra recognized Councilor Fresolo, who discussed the process relative to 
offset costs associated with taking out an additional bond without raising taxes with the Chief 
Financial Officer. 
November 9, 2026 Page 5 of 12Municipal and Legislative Operations Committee
Chairperson Councilor Mitra recognized Councilor Rosen and Councilor Bergman, who spoke 
concerning the item with the Deputy City Clerk. 
Chairperson Councilor Mitra brought forth the following Chairman’s Order on a roll call vote of 3 
Yeas and 0 Nays: “Request City Manager consider implementing a City Council budget priority 
process to ensure Councilors are able to provide the City Manager with each of their budgetary 
priorities in a timely and transparent manner, each City Department thru the City Manager, as listed 
in Appendix B of the Rules of the City Council, shall hereby submit a semiannual performance 
evaluation report to the Council for referral to each appropriate Standing Committee on or before 
January 1 of each year. Each performance evaluation report shall include the department’s specific , 
measurable, attainable, relevant and timebound (SMART) goals and objectives, as well as their prior 
year budget information. Following the review of the various performance evaluation reports and 
based on public feedback received from residents, Councilors may, on or before February 15 of each 
year, provide their budget priorities and recommendations to the City Manager for consideration in 
preparing the upcoming fiscal year’s budget. Said recommendations may include, but shall not be 
limited to, proposed projects, programs, service improvements, operational needs and policy 
initiatives. After analyzing the priorities given by the Councilors, the City Manager, shall submit a 
preliminary budget report to the City Council on or before March 15 of each year for referral to the 
Standing Committee on Finance. Said report shall identify the administration’s budget priorities for 
the upcoming fiscal year and shall include anticipated proposed projects, programs, service 
improvements, operation needs, and policy initiatives that shall be proposed in the official fiscal year 
budget.”
Chairperson Councilor Mitra moved for a roll call vote to recommend the item be placed on file. 
Recommend File on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays

Order of Councilor Jose A. Rivera - Request Standing Committee on Municipal and 
Legislative Operations review the Rules of the City Council relative to public participation 
to discuss the feasibility of amending the Rules of City Council to have all City Council 
meetings begin at either 5:30 p.m. or 6 p.m., with public participation occurring from the 
set time of either 5:30 p.m. to 6:30 p.m. or 6 p.m. to 7 p.m. each meeting.
# 11b CC October 13, 2026
a.
November 9, 2026 Page 8 of 12Municipal and Legislative Operations Committee
Chairperson Councilor Mitra read the item and recognized Councilor Rivera, who spoke concerning 
the item. 
Chairperson Councilor Mitra recognized Councilor Bergman, who discussed the feasibility of 
convening City Council at 5:30 p.m. with public participation at 6:30 p.m. with the ability to take up 
items out of order that are not anticipated to be items of public interest with Councilor Rivera. 
Chairperson Councilor Mitra recognized Councilor Rosen, who discussed potential challenges 
relative to assuming which agenda items are of public interest, highlighted the benefits relative to 
facilitating public participation at the beginning of meetings, that standing committee meetings 
convening between 5:00 p.m. and 5:30 p.m., and how communities such as Boston convene their City 
Council meetings around 12:00 p.m.
Chairperson Councilor Mitra recognized Councilor Bergman, who discussed benefits of convening 
City Council before 6:30 p.m. and that the School Committee convenes at 5:00 p.m.
Chairperson Councilor Mitra recognized Councilor Rosen, who spoke concerning the amount of 
residents who remain in attendance for City Council meetings past public participation. 
Chairperson Councilor Mitra discussed facilitating City Council meetings as they currently are but 
convening at an earlier time with Councilor Rivera. 
Chairperson Councilor Mitra recognized Councilor Bergman, who discussed allocating up to one (1) 
hour for public participation with the understanding that the full hour may or may not be used in its 
entirety by the public.
Chairperson Councilor Mitra discussed amending the Rules of City Council to strike “ 6:30” from 
Rule 4 and replace it with “ 5:30” and to strike “thirty (30)” from Rule 39 and replace it with “sixty 
(60)” with the City Clerk. 
Chairperson Councilor Mitra then brought forth the following two (2) Chairman’s Orders: 1) That the 
Rules of City Council of the City of Worcester be and are hereby amended to amend Rule 4 to read 
as follows: Rule 4. Regular Meetings. Regular meetings of the city council shall be held weekly on 
Tuesday evenings at 5:30 o’clock p .m. in the council chamber located inside City Hall, unless at a 
previous meeting, by a majority vote, the city council determines another day, time and /or place . 
Notwithstanding the above, the mayor may advance the starting time for any regular meeting to any 
time no earlier than 4:00 p.m. to accommodate an extraordinarily long agenda, a request by the city 
manager to schedule an executive session, or for any other suitable reason. In such event the mayor 
shall cause notice of the advanced time to be delivered to each member of the city council no later 
than the time for posting the meeting agenda; and 2) That the Rules of City Council of the City of 
Worcester be and are hereby amended to amend Rule 39 to read as follows: Rule 39. Items of Public 
Interest. At every meeting of the city council, under the "public participation" portion of the agenda , 
the chair shall recognize any person seeking such recognition for the purpose of addressing the 
council on any eligible item on the agenda for that meeting both in person and remotely. Any person 
who wishes to speak on more than one agenda item shall combine their testimony on all items to one 
appearance at the microphone. The time for speaking shall not exceed two minutes for any one 
speaker or sixty (60) minutes for all speakers. This privilege shall not apply to items “held under 
November 9, 2026 Page 9 of 12Municipal and Legislative Operations Committee
privilege.” This privilege shall also not apply to items listed on the agenda as pending in the 
committee on finance and/or ordinances or to tabled items.”
Chairperson Councilor Mitra moved for a roll call vote to recommend the item be placed on file. 
Recommend File on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays

That the Rules of City Council of the City of Worcester be and are hereby amended to

chamber located inside City Hall, unless at a previous meeting, by a majority vote, the city

That the Rules of City Council of the City of Worcester be and are hereby amended to 
amend Rule 39 to read as follows: Rule 39. Items of Public Interest. At every meeting of 
the city council, under the "public participation" portion of the agenda, the chair shall 
recognize any person seeking such recognition for the purpose of addressing the council 
on any eligible item on the agenda for that meeting both in person and remotely. Any

two minutes for any one speaker or sixty (60) minutes for all speakers. This privilege shall 
not apply to items “held under privilege .” This privilege shall also not apply to items listed 
on the agenda as pending in the committee on finance and /or ordinances or to tabled 
items.
